title: Germany 30-Year Bund multi-ISIN auction (EUR 2.5bn across two reopening lines) — on FOMC day
source: EST: deutsche-finanzagentur.de English issuance calendar (/en/federal-securities/issuances/issuance-calendar), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 125,468 bytes) — the Quarter III 2026 table lists TWO 30-year reopening lines dated 16.09.2026: 'Bund 30 Y (R)' at EUR 1.0bn with the ISIN shown as '-', and 'Bund (R)' DE000BU2D012, coupon 2.90%, maturity 15.08.2056, at EUR 1.5bn. Corroborated by two further Finanzagentur primaries fetched the same session: the auction-process page (/en/federal-securities/issuances/auction-process, HTTP 200, 96,570 bytes), which states that nominal Bunds of 7 years or more are 'always held on Wednesdays' (16.09.2026 is a Wednesday), that auctions and multi-ISIN auctions are 'announced four bank business days before the auction date by press notice', and that for 15/30-year multi-ISIN auctions 'the second bond ... [is] only announced in a press notice in the week before the auction' — which is why the EUR 1.0bn line carries no ISIN; and the issuance-history workbook (emissionshistorie_en.xlsx, 351,323 bytes, 'Auction Results since 1999', 2,143 auctions), which shows DE000BU2D012 reopened twelve times since 2025-04-16, always as part of a multi-ISIN ('M-A') 30-year auction. The four-business-day rule is observable rather than merely stated: the 09.09.2026 Bund reopening was announced on 2026-09-03. Stays `estimate` on one mechanical count, not on date doubt: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:), the same limit jgb-20y-auction-2026-09-15 and ecb-decision-2026-09-10 both recorded. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Discovered during the treasury-30y-bond-2026-09-10 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08) and researched 2026-09-09 (docs/research/events/bund-30y-auction-2026-09-16.md); this canonical file replaces the proposal it arrived as. Germany sells EUR 2.5bn of 30-year duration on the FOMC's September decision day, with bidding closing 11:30 local (09:30 UTC = 05:30 ET) — about 8.5 hours before the 2:00pm ET statement. Tiered `low` and NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: no house playbook is rates-keyed and no tracked symbol carries euro-rates exposure. The initial research tested the spillover directly and returned a null on both legs — across 213 German 30Y auction dates 2003-01-01 to 2026-08-26, soft-vs-firm bid-to-offer moved the US 30Y CMT by -0.04bp (t = -0.06) and the Bundesbank 30Y by +0.35bp (t = +0.66); the sharper cut, the 47 dates where total bids came in below the offered volume, gave +0.25bp US (t = +0.30) and +1.04bp Bund (t = +1.60) against daily standard deviations of 4.94 and 3.90bp. It also corrected the proposal's own 'the FOMC dominates' premise: 25 of those 213 dates (11.7%) were FOMC decision days, and on them the US 30Y's mean absolute move was 3.17bp, SMALLER than the 3.87bp on non-FOMC auction dates. What the entry buys is therefore attribution and a checkable expectation, not signal: a 09-16 long-end move is not automatically the Fed's, and the auction's allotment (~EUR 2.04bn at the 2022-26 30Y retention rate of 18.6%) is computable in advance where the wire copy will be about the dot plot. Two structural facts govern how the result must be read. (1) A 'failed Bund auction' headline is a format artifact: Germany runs a multi-price auction and retains part of every issue for secondary-market use (Finanzagentur's own published table: 21.5% of auction volume in 2025), which put bids under the offer on 22.1% of 30Y dates since 2003 and on 3 of 16 in 2026. (2) Germany is the mirror image of Japan on super-long supply — 30Y gross auction supply went EUR 11.4bn (2022) to 32.5, 27.5 and 37.0bn (2025), roughly a tripling, while jgb-20y-auction-2026-09-15 measured Japan cutting its 20Y and 40Y by 30-40%. The 23.09.2026 Bund 15Y on the same calendar is recorded here and not filed: wrong tenor for this ledger's question. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
